item.title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan
item.description: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan condemned the extensive deletion of voter names from electoral rolls due to the special intensive revision process. He emphasized that such actions undermine the core principles of the Indian Constitution and disenfranchise millions of citizens. Bhuyan highlighted that the right to vote is essential for free and fair elections in India. He urged that no citizen should be denied the right to vote without due process.
item.dc:creator: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA

item.title: Flydubai co-pilot allegedly tried to crash plane after hijack attempt failed
item.description: An Omani co-pilot attacked the captain of a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv. Following the assault, he attempted to crash the aircraft into the Saudi desert. Investigators are looking into whether the co-pilot cut the engines' fuel supply during this crisis. Emergency codes were transmitted to air traffic control indicating both a general emergency and a suspected hijacking.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: US withdraws all bombers from UK's Fairford base after suspected terror plot
item.description: The United States has withdrawn all bombers from RAF Fairford following an investigation into a suspected terror plot. The withdrawal occurred shortly after several people were arrested in connection with the alleged attack plans. British authorities indicated potential Iranian involvement, while Tehran firmly denied these claims and summoned the British ambassador. Additionally, the US maintains military presence in the Middle East with several ships heading to the region.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Faster registration, easier refunds: Reform rollout with GST 2.0
item.description: GST Council plans to unveil substantial reforms aimed at improving business processes and facilitating growth. The proposed changes involve streamlined registration, easier refunds, and a more efficient input tax credit system. Decriminalisation measures are also proposed to alleviate issues for businesses with minor offenses. A focus is on reducing discretionary practices and using technology to minimize litigation. These reforms seek to enhance operational efficiency for both small and large enterprises.
item.dc:creator: SIDHARTHA

item.title: Other side of Sept 30: A family waited anxiously for their son — Capt Smit Machchhar
item.description: Captain Smit Machchhar was injured during a terrorist attack and underwent surgery in a military hospital. His parents initially faced uncertainty regarding his condition while trying to reach him. After being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, Smit's father felt relieved upon visiting him. The family decided to focus on Smit's recovery instead of revisiting the traumatic event. They remain optimistic about his healing process and future homecoming.
item.dc:creator: HEMALI CHHAPIA AND MANJU V

item.title: Marc Benioff, wife gave $100M to UCSF; 5 years later, children’s hospital opened
item.description: In 2010, Marc Benioff and Lynne Benioff contributed $100 million to build a new children's hospital at UCSF. Five years later, UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital San Francisco officially opened with 183 beds for pediatric care. Before the hospital's opening, the Benioffs donated an additional $100 million to enhance healthcare services and research. The design prioritized family-centered care, including rooms for parents and outdoor recovery spaces.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: West Bengal: Laws in 6 months to end ‘land jihad’, ‘love jihad’, says CM Suvendu
item.description: Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced plans to implement the Uniform Civil Code. This initiative follows similar efforts in Uttarakhand and Gujarat, which recently received presidential assent. A committee led by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai is drafting the proposed laws, with public hearings scheduled across five divisions. The committee aims to gather feedback from the public and rights bodies on the matter.
item.dc:creator: DIPAWALI MITRA AND ROHIT KHANNA

item.title: Texas city to pay at least $175,000 over excess groundwater pumping at SpaceX site
item.description: The McGregor City Council has reached a settlement regarding penalties related to groundwater overpumping caused by SpaceX. The city will allocate $175,000 for this resolution and commit to a 25-year groundwater monitoring program. However, residents are concerned about who will bear these costs, urging that SpaceX should take financial responsibility.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 'Avengers: Endgame' dethrones 'Avatar' as highest-grossing film of all time
item.description: Avengers: Endgame has reclaimed its position as the highest-grossing film following a re-release. The film surpassed Avatar's total box office earnings by a narrow margin after its Encore re-release. Despite a drop to seventh place domestically, additional earnings helped Endgame regain the crown. Marvel Studios expressed gratitude to fans for their support through social media messages. The success of Endgame coincides with anticipation for the upcoming film Avengers: Doomsday.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Man bought Goodwill painting for $3; it later sold for $190,000
item.description: In a remarkable twist of fate, a former antiques dealer purchased a painting for just $3, suspecting it held greater value. Appraisers on Antiques Roadshow estimated its worth between $20,000 and $30,000, but the auction result astonished everyone, fetching $190,000. This stunning Flemish piece, dating back to around 1650, serves as a testament to the hidden gems that can be discovered in thrift shops and donation centers.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Meet Nathan Montelongo, seventh-grader who used shellfish waste to clean water
item.description: Nathan Gael Montelongo, a seventh-grader from La Joya, Texas, created a project using chitosan. He collected discarded shellfish shells to produce chitosan powder and tested its effectiveness on polluted water. Studies showed that chitosan improved water clarity and benefited zebrafish embryos in experiments. Nathan designed a prototype raft that could automate water quality monitoring and treatment.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: MacKenzie Scott gave $30M to housing nonprofit; a year later, it unveiled 10-year plan
item.description: MacKenzie Scott has made headlines with her unprecedented $30 million donation to Housing Trust Silicon Valley, marking the organization's largest-ever gift. This investment is set to bolster affordable housing options throughout the Bay Area, as the trust plans to enhance its loan fund and expand various housing initiatives over the next decade.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Mississippi couple wins $41,920 after loggers cut 1,299 trees on their land
item.description: In a significant logging error, 1,299 trees were cut down on Gerald and Rhonda Smith's property in Mississippi. The Smiths meticulously recorded the extent of their loss through photographs and measurements, leading to legal proceedings. A court recognized the logging company's blatant negligence, awarding the couple $41,920. Expert surveyor J.T. Strickland confirmed the boundary lines, and the appeals court reaffirmed the lower court’s ruling, validating the Smiths' claims for damages.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Ex-SC judge Nariman
item.description: Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman expressed concerns regarding the functioning of the Election Commission in India. He highlighted the issue of illegal removal of voters from electoral lists, especially in West Bengal. Nariman noted that 90 lakh voters were disenfranchised, with many not having access to justice. He emphasized the need for reform in the appointment process of election commissioners to ensure fairness.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine
item.description: In Ukraine's Sumy region, six Russian drones attacked the Kusum Group's pharmaceutical plant, killing one engineer and injuring others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed during the targeted strike, which occurs amid a pattern of similar attacks. The company estimates damage from this incident could exceed $50 million, impacting operations significantly.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: Lewis Hamilton sells $43.9 million NYC penthouse for $49.5 million
item.description: Lewis Hamilton bought the 8,908-square-foot Penthouse H at 443 Greenwich Street for $43.99 million in 2017 but never lived there. He listed it for $57 million in 2019 before it entered contract at $49.5 million in 2021. The sale gave him a gross gain of about $5.5 million, while Jennifer Gates was later linked to the property.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Andy Reid reveals what makes Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes different
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid shares more about Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes ahead of facing the Las Vegas Raiders.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: EAM Jaishankar says US has chosen to become 'lonelier power'
item.description: S Jaishankar stated that India aims to mediate in the Russia-Ukraine conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. India has recently proposed ideas addressing issues like grain and energy exports to both nations. Jaishankar emphasized America's changing global position and the implications of China's rise on international relations. India is also facing domestic repercussions due to the ongoing conflict, including commercial shipping disruptions.
item.dc:creator: SACHIN PARASHAR

item.title: 'Look Out Circular' against parents of man who secretly took away child to US
item.description: The Supreme Court has indicated consequences for parents of a man who abducted his daughter to the US. This decision came during a case regarding child custody between NRI couples. The father has been ordered to return to India with the child within four weeks. If he fails to comply, his parents will face legal consequences. The court emphasizes the importance of the child's connection with her mother.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: 25p/kg wheat MSP hike an 'insult': Samyukta Kisan Morcha
item.description: Farmer organisations represented by Samyukta Kisan Morcha rejected the government's announced minimum support prices for Rabi crops. They described the small increase for wheat as an insult rather than acceptable compensation. SKM called for a revision of MSPs and urged states to offer bonuses to farmers. Additionally, they highlighted the impact of rising diesel and input costs on farming.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: From India to Australia: How 6 countries got caught up in flydubai terror
item.description: On September 30, the flydubai Flight FZ1073 faced a cockpit attack when Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar. The injured pilot bravely opened the cockpit door, allowing crew and passengers to subdue the co-pilot. The flight was diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where al-Hammami was apprehended by authorities. Investigations have since been undertaken by several countries into al-Hammami’s background and possible extremist ties.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: 'More involved': EAM confirms India has 'gone beyond advocacy' to end Ukraine war
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: UK: 2 teenagers jailed for 10 years for arson at Indian restaurant in London
item.description: Two 17-year-old teenagers were sentenced to 10 years for an arson attack at Indian Aroma. The incident occurred on August 22, 2025, when they threatened diners with weapons. Their actions led to severe burns for multiple victims, including a couple who suffered life-threatening injuries. The court emphasized the planning and intent behind the attack, which resulted in serious harm. The motive for this violent act remains unknown.
item.dc:creator: NAOMI CANTON

item.title: ‘Thanks for the gift’: Pant’s 29th birthday made special as RoI reclaim Irani Cup
item.description: Rishabh Pant's birthday happened to coincide with a remarkable comeback as the Rest of India triumphed over Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup. Despite falling behind initially, the team rallied to secure a 167-run victory. Although Pant missed the action due to illness, he joined in the post-match festivities. Mukesh Kumar's exceptional bowling and young talent Ravichandran Smaran's innings were pivotal.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Kashmiri teacher fights period stigma, one village at a time
item.description: Aasima Jan works diligently in north Kashmir, focusing on menstrual health awareness to help girls stay in school. She began her efforts after witnessing the stigma around menstruation affecting attendance rates among female students. Monthly sessions in villages educate families about menstrual hygiene and encourage open discussion about the topic. Aasima also distributes sanitary pads, highlighting their importance for health and hygiene.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: 'I do not accept': Chavan rejects Raj Thackeray’s poll boycott call amid SIR row
item.dc:creator: SUBHADRA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Pakistani prisoner dies by suicide in jail
item.description: Shahid Imran, a 36-year-old Pakistani undertrial prisoner, was found unconscious in his jail cell early Sunday. He was a resident of Sargooda district in Punjab, Pakistan. Authorities rushed him to GMCH where doctors declared him brought dead. The incident occurred at the high-security central jail in Jammu. An investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death is likely to follow.
item.dc:creator: SANJAY KHAJURIA

item.title: Asian Games: PM Modi congratulates Team India, hails ‘passion and sporting spirit’
item.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the inspiring performances of Indian athletes at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, where India clinched a remarkable total of 85 medals, including 21 golds, finishing fourth overall. The Games were highlighted by record-breaking efforts, particularly in athletics, showcasing the talent of emerging athletes. Modi called for enhanced focus on grassroots sports development to empower future generations.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Sharad Sagar left US to work in India; years later, White House invited him back
item.description: After studying in the US, Sharad Vivek Sagar decided to return to Bihar, despite his friends' disbelief. They teased him, challenging his choice, and he quipped that only a White House invitation would lure him back. Years later, his dedication to education earned him an invite from Barack Obama, turning a light-hearted jest into reality and representing his commitment to his home state.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Asian Games: PT Usha names Kumkum Mohod, Sujeet Kalkal as Team India’s MVPs
item.description: At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, Kumkum Mohod and Sujeet Kalkal shone brightly, capturing the spotlight with their remarkable achievements. Mohod clinched three medals, including two golds, breaking South Korea's stronghold in archery. Meanwhile, Kalkal staged an impressive comeback to win gold in men's 65kg freestyle wrestling. Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha lauded their tenacity, announcing plans to celebrate their triumphs in an upcoming ceremony.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.description: Messi moved to Barcelona as a teenager. While Spain tried to convince him to play for them, Argentina had limited knowledge of the youngster from Rosario.

item.title: 'It’s about time': Jaffer backs left-haned batter as Kohli's replacement at No.3
item.description: Kohli has confirmed that the 2027 edition will be his last ODI World Cup for India, meaning the team will have to find a replacement at No. 3, a position he has held for many years.
item.dc:creator: SHUBHANSHU DWIVEDI

item.title: ‘Beti Bachao Delhi Police Se!’: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke on Neha Bora’s detention
item.description: Members of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) protested near Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. During the protest, AISA president Neha Bora was reportedly detained by the Delhi Police in a vehicle. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) workers, including Saurabh Bhardwaj, were also detained while protesting at India Gate. Bhardwaj alleged mistreatment by officers during his detention, questioning the treatment of the common man.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: Jio Platforms IPO likely by Oct-end; $3.8 bn issue, $143-146 bn company valuation: Report
item.description: Jio Platforms is preparing for its stock market debut with an estimated issue size of $3.8 billion, which could set records. The IPO aims for a valuation of $143-146 billion, with filings expected in mid-October. Reliance Jio’s expansion includes telecom, cloud, AI, and services, reporting significant financial growth recently. Past investors include tech giants like Meta and Google, contributing substantial capital to the company.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: 'Pulled out dagger’: 'Drunk' driver attacks BJP MLA in Assam; 2 home guards injured
item.description: A truck driver attacked BJP MLA Ritu Baran Sarmah outside his office in Guwahati and created chaos. The driver, believed to be intoxicated, rammed a parked vehicle belonging to party workers. Sarmah stated that the police initially handled the situation, but it escalated when the driver brandished a dagger. During the confrontation, two home guards sustained injuries while trying to intervene.
item.dc:creator: TATHAGATA BHATTACHARJEE

item.title: Yeh Rishta actor Mohsin Khan gets married to Tamanna
item.description: Mohsin Khan recently shared a delightful snapshot from his wedding festivities alongside Tamanna, creating quite a stir among fans. The photo, captioned 'The Day MashaAllah,' was met with excitement. Shortly after, videos of the couple enjoying a dance together emerged online. Following their engagement in August, Mohsin affectionately called her his 'Person,' prompting an outpouring of congratulations from admirers.

item.title: ‘Learn and keep moving forward’: Bindra’s message to Team India as LA 2028 beckons
item.description: After the Asian Games, Abhinav Bindra called for a revolution in high-performance systems for Indian athletes. While acknowledging India’s notable successes, he insisted on a careful assessment of both triumphs and failures. With the Los Angeles Olympics approaching, Bindra pointed out the necessity of stable athlete growth and targeted training.
